stories.headline: Caleb Wilson and a new regime: The summer that changed the Chicago Bulls
stories.summary: It has been an offseason of change in Chicago. Now, No. 4 pick Caleb Wilson and a new Bulls front office have turned the tide for a franchise lost in the middle.
stories.body:
IT'S AUG. 22 and Chicago Bulls fans pack the area surrounding the United Center. The team is hosting its annual two-day fan festival, Bulls fest, and fans are lining up for the chance to meet the 20-year-old who has not only provided a new, unfamiliar hope around the franchise this summer but someone to pull the franchise out of a decade of irrelevance. This is Caleb Wilson's introduction to Chicago.

The lines for his meet-and-greet wrap around the atrium. The next event of the fest is a slam dunk contest in the parking lot, where Wilson is one of the judges. But first, he screams and sticks his tongue out for a hype video in front of a crowd of fans standing in front of the Michael Jordan statue.

The image -- a juxtaposition from where the franchise once was and where it now plans to go -- is impossible to ignore.

The anticipation has been growing for months, ever since the Bulls selected the North Carolina star No. 4 overall during the NBA draft in June.

The Bulls hope Wilson is the new face of the franchise, a much-needed refresh for a team that has missed the playoffs in eight of the past nine seasons.

The hype began to boil after Wilson's electric showing during his first in-game action at the Las Vegas summer league. Wilson finished his first professional game with 35 points, the second-highest total for a rookie debut in summer league history, and knocked down seven 3-pointers in the process.

In his second game, Wilson soared over 6-foot-11 Jazz center Jonas Aidoo to throw down an emphatic dunk in one of the top highlight-reel plays of the summer.

By his fourth and final game, Hall of Fame forward Kevin Garnett sat courtside to get a glimpse of the rookie to whom he started to draw comparisons. Both are 6-foot-10, wiry 215-pound players buoyed by elite athleticism. "I actually think his floor is Kevin Garnett," Warriors forward Draymond Green said on his podcast this summer.

"And man, if that's your floor, oh my god. Do you know how great KG was? I actually think with Caleb Wilson, Kevin Garnett could be his floor. That's how special I think Caleb Wilson is."

Teams are normally hesitant to make grand proclamations from summer league, but Wilson's performance stood out.

"He looks," one team source told ESPN, "like we got a dude."

The Bulls believe Wilson is yet another new pillar of an almost entirely new leadership structure. They hired a new head of basketball operations, Bryson Graham, who had a reputation for building through the draft and finding young talent.

Graham then selected a new head coach, Tiago Splitter, who has a background of player development success stories. They selected Wilson and then rounded out the roster with veterans such as Norman Powell and Nic Claxton, but Wilson's development will be the franchise's top priority in the 2026-27 season.

"We just want to see internal growth from our young guys and even from our veteran players," Graham told ESPN. "We just want to see a team that's going to go out there, represent this city well, play hard and obviously continue to grow and continue to develop."

Though expectations are high for Wilson across the league, team sources said there is no pressure for the Bulls to compete for a play-in or playoff spot in a loaded Eastern Conference. After years of the Bulls trying to jump-start themselves back into relevance, the decision-makers in Chicago are preaching patience before a resurrection.

For his part, though, Wilson has made his goals for his rookie season clear.

"I expect to have Rookie of the Year, honestly," Wilson said. "I'm going to work hard. I'm going to do what it takes. I feel like the team is really good for me and how I envision to play."

THE SUMMER LEAGUE debut was eye-popping in a smaller, but even more tantalizing, way.

Wilson's seven made 3s were more than he made during his entire freshman season at North Carolina.

Concerns about his shooting ability -- along with an injury that shortened his college season and kept him out of the NCAA tournament -- were the biggest knocks against him entering the draft and why he was ultimately selected behind AJ Dybantsa, Darryn Peterson and Cameron Boozer in the 2026 draft class.

To explain and perhaps ease those concerns, Wilson pointed to the system at North Carolina, one that did not ask him to take 3-pointers (he averaged 1.1 attempts per game), but he also noted how he began working to improve his shot once the college season ended.

"I'm glad I didn't shoot 3s in college," Wilson said after a practice this summer. "Because if I did, I wouldn't be here. I don't know where I'd be. I don't think I'd be a Bull."

A broken thumb and left wrist fracture ended Wilson's college season in February, and he couldn't move his thumb while wearing a cast that kept the digit straight. But he could still hold a ball to practice his form, and he did so -- over and over, all summer.

Wilson estimates he has been shooting between 2,000 and 2,500 3-pointers per day.

For as much as Wilson's performance on the court generated buzz throughout the league, his work ethic has only heightened the excitement inside the organization.

He cried before his professional debut, five months to the day since the end of his college season, because he said he had been waiting for that moment for so long. The other top picks in his class were shut down from action after two or three summer league games, but Wilson pushed to keep playing, texting Graham to ask to play on the second night of a back-to-back in Chicago's third game of the summer.

Wilson averaged 23.5 points, 7.3 rebounds, 1.3 steals and 2.5 blocks in four summer league games at and was named to the all-summer league first team. When informed that his 35-point debut was one of the highest-scoring debut performances in the history of the event, Wilson shrugged it off because his team lost.

Outside of his time in Las Vegas, Wilson has been a mainstay in Chicago since the draft. He works out at the team's practice facility in the morning and then returns around 8 or 9 p.m., along with fellow first-round pick Dailyn Swain, who was selected No. 15 by Chicago in June, for workouts that routinely approach midnight.

"Everybody highlights his athleticism, which is generational," Swain said. "But he can do a lot of things. He's really good facing up at the elbow, jab. He has a really good midrange shot. He's been knocking down 3s, so he's widening his arsenal."

GRAHAM'S FIRST MAJOR hire as the team's head of basketball operations was to bring in Splitter, a coach whose vision Graham touted as close to his own.

As an interim coach last season, Splitter led the Portland Trail Blazers to a surprise playoff appearance as the No. 7 seed in the Western Conference, but during his introductory news conference in Chicago, neither Splitter nor Graham focused on repeating such an unlikely jump.

Graham touted Splitter's player development credentials, from helping Deni Avdija become an All-Star in Portland to his days as an assistant coach, guiding Jarrett Allen as a member of the Brooklyn Nets' player development staff in 2019 or a young Alperen Sengun as an assistant with the Houston Rockets in 2023.

"The first thing you do is connect," Splitter said. "That's the foundation of everything you do, especially at this level. If you don't have that, it's really hard to demand and make them respect you. The foundation is [to] connect with the players in different ways."

Splitter started his bond with Wilson early this summer. It began with a shared interest in music and with Splitter being surprised at Wilson's range in music tastes. The 19-year-old began learning the guitar in his spare time this summer and has played everything from hip-hop to classical to country.

"Very interesting young guy," Splitter said. "You see how his brain functions and the variety of things he can have a conversation about."

Splitter also stepped in to coach the Bulls at summer league for the team's first two games in Las Vegas. He said he wanted the opportunity to establish a culture with his young players. For a young coach still finding his identity, it was good practice for the challenge of taking over a franchise starved for a winner with newfound expectations of the future.

"He's really detailed," Wilson said. "He knows what he wants you to do and he's pretty serious. Most coaches, you have coaches that are joking around and stuff like that. Tiago's pretty serious and he knows what he wants.

"I'd rather have someone who's serious and straightforward with me, so I know what I can do better."

Wilson functioned as the team's point guard and primary ball handler for most of the summer -- something that wasn't featured in Garnett's Hall of Fame career -- but those duties will lessen by the start of the season when he's surrounded by Josh Giddey, Powell and third-year forward Matas Buzelis, who will help run the offense after starting 77 games last season.

"It builds a healthy environment," Graham said. "It gives the younger guys confidence, too, because they know that, when it is going bad, they have some guys that have done it, some guys that have won and had success and they can learn. It's just really important for the overall development of our younger players and the health of our team."

In his previous experiences as a head coach, Splitter has been malleable in his style of play.

He coached in France and led Paris Basketball, a club in the first division of French basketball, to the EuroLeague playoffs with a fast-paced offense.

With the Blazers a season ago, defense became the calling card. Chicago represents his first chance to shape a young roster in his own image.

"You have to adapt your system to the players you have," Splitter said.

"Yes, I have a vision. I have a certain way I want to play, but you also have to explore what they do best. That's what we're going to do here."

It's what Splitter was hired to accomplish -- to help nurture and guide Chicago's roster while its young players develop.

In what has become an annual tradition, Bulls players convened in Miami last week for a player-run minicamp a few weeks before training camp.

And as the hype for Wilson continues to rise, the Bulls rookie remains focused on his ultimate goal.

"I do expect to win," he said. "Whatever it takes to win is what I'm going to do."

stories.headline: What can we expect on transfer deadline day? Balogun, Enzo, Álvarez updates?
stories.summary: The summer transfer deadline closes on Sept. 1 at 6 p.m. ET for the Premier League, so here's a few things that could still happen.
stories.body:
Enzo Fernández, Julián Álvarez, Folarin Balogun and Cody Gakpo -- it sounds like a list of big performers at the 2026 Men's World Cup, but fast-forward six weeks from that tournament, and they are the leading names that could seal headline moves on transfer deadline day.

By the time the summer window closes at 11 p.m. BST / 6 p.m. ET on Sept. 1, Premier League spending alone is likely to go past the £2.5 billion mark due to the magnitude of the deals that could still be done; a huge figure, but still short of last summer's £3.1 billion total outlay.

Manchester City's pursuit of Chelsea midfielder Fernández, who was a Premier League record transfer when he arrived at Stamford Bridge from Benfica for £106.8 million in January 2023, could see the Argentina international break the Premier League record again if Chelsea force City to exceed the £125 million figure that Liverpool paid to sign striker Alexander Isak from Newcastle 12 months ago.

City have already smashed their own transfer record this summer by completing a £116 million move for Nottingham Forest midfielder Elliot Anderson, but sources have said that Chelsea want a higher fee than that to land the 25-year-old Fernández, so the numbers will go only higher and higher.

If Chelsea, as expected, sanction Fernández's departure, then manager Xabi Alonso will move for Monaco's £40 million-rated Lamine Camara as his midfield replacement. But City, who signed Morocco's World Cup breakout star Ayyoub Bouaddi in an £86 million deal from Lille last week, won't restrict their business just to signing Fernández.

Talks are ongoing with Liverpool over a potential £85 million deal for Netherlands forward Cody Gakpo -- a transfer unlocked by Liverpool agreeing a £123 million deal for Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola -- and Gakpo's arrival at the Etihad will enable winger Jack Grealish to take his pick of a loan move back to one of his two former teams: Everton or Aston Villa.

Everton manager David Moyes challenged his board to deliver more signings last week, and the message appears to have had an effect because the Blues are closing in on a deal to re-sign Richarlison from Tottenham, will Iliman Ndiaye heading the other way to Spurs in two separate transfers rather than a swap deal.

Moyes wants to bolster his attacking options, and he retains a strong interest in USMNT forward Balogun, but Everton will need to offload Beto to enable them to raise the finances to complete a €40 million move for the Monaco striker.

Forwards are often the big movers on deadline day due to clubs wanting to give themselves the insurance policy of proven goals for the season ahead. But it will take some impressive negotiations by Arsenal to convince Atlético Madrid to allow long-term target Julian Álvarez to leave the Metropolitano for the Emirates.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has been pursuing Álvarez since early last season, but Atleti have been resolute in their stance that the former Manchester City forward will not get his wish of a move to Barcelona.

Álvarez finally returned to training with Diego Simeone's squad over the weekend following a standoff with the club over his future, so the Argentina forward might now have accepted that he will not leave during this window. But sources have said that Atletico could be tempted to offload Álvarez to Arsenal if Viktor Gyökeres moves in the opposite direction, so that box office deal could yet happen before the deadline.

If it does, Arsenal might need to balance their finances after a busy summer that has seen them sign Newcastle's Bruno Guimarães (£75 million) and Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa (£51 million), so it could raise the prospect of a surprise deadline day move for homegrown youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Arteta was adamant earlier this month that the versatile 19-year-old, who can operate at left back and in midfield, would not leave the Gunners, but Arsenal CEO Richard Garlick left the door open by admitting the club could be forced to consider offers if the "right opportunity" arose.

Chelsea and Manchester United are both interested in Lewis-Skelly and would be ready to make a late move if Arsenal suddenly displayed a readiness to do business, but right now, Lewis-Skelly looks more likely to remain at the Emirates.

United have also monitored Newcastle's Lewis Hall in their search for an upgrade on left back Luke Shaw, but the former Chelsea youngster is expected to stay at St James' Park. Having spent a relatively modest £148 million so far to land three midfielders (Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba) and a back-up goalkeeper (Karl Darlow), United are expected to be quiet on deadline day unless they can find a left back.

But United forward Joshua Zirkzee is likely to move out on loan, with Juventus and Fiorentina both interested in the former Bologna player.

Fenerbahce have a long-standing interest in Marcus Rashford, but United manager Michael Carrick has brought the England forward back into the fold following loan spells at Barcelona and Aston Villa and only a huge offer would now tempt United to part with the 28-year-old.

Spurs did have an interest in Rashford earlier in the window, but Roberto De Zerbi's team has completed other business and their efforts are now focused on finding clubs for Kevin Danso, Richarlison and Pape Matar Sarr.

Sunderland are in talks for Danso and Richarlison is heading back to Everton, while Juventus are negotiating for Sarr.

If Spurs can finalize all of those outgoings early enough, they may chase one more attacking signing -- they will move for Gakpo if City fail to seal a deal with Liverpool, and have also been linked with AC Milan's USMNT star Christian Pulisic -- but the likelihood is that the revolving door at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will see more exits than arrivals.

But with the clock ticking down to the deadline, the biggest focus will be on Argentina pair Fernández and Álvarez; Fernández is almost certain to happen, while Álvarez is an outside bet.

It's transfer deadline day, so don't rule anything out.

stories.headline: Concussion saga not a distraction for finals-bound Cats
stories.summary: Geelong players are adamant the AFL club's concussion saga hasn't been a distraction as the Cats gear up for finals while relishing Jake Kolodjashnij's return to the fold.
stories.body:
Geelong players are adamant the AFL club's concussion saga hasn't been a distraction as the Cats gear up for finals while relishing Jake Kolodjashnij's return to the fold.

The Cats were last week fined $140,000 for failing to officially let the AFL know about the concussion waiver in Kolodjashnij's contract.

The penalty is $100,000 plus a suspended sanction of $40,000, which stems from the league fining Geelong last October after an investigation into the club's third-party agreements.

Kolodjashnij, who came forward as the player involved shortly after the story broke and has not played at any level since, returned to the club last week ahead of the finals.

When asked about Kolodjashnij's return, midfielder Tom Atkins, the defender's 2022 premiership teammate, said: "Awesome. Kola's one of my favourite teammates, so yeah, to see him back, feeling a bit better.

"Obviously we'd love him to be back playing and back in training, but hopefully that can get itself sorted soon.

"But just having him in the rooms and seeing him smiling again is good."

Asked on Monday whether he or another player had a discussion around a similar concussion agreement, Atkins said: "No".

The experienced midfielder indicated the concussion saga, and last week's handing down of a fine, hadn't been discussed with the players.

"No, it's very much been, our focus has been performing on the weekends, and yeah, we just wanted to make sure Kola was alright as teammates and as friends," Atkins said.

"That's probably the extent of the detail that we looked into it as players. So yeah, just care for Kola, that's pretty much it."

Geelong start their September campaign in Friday night's blockbuster elimination final against Carlton at the MCG.

Asked whether the concussion saga had been a distraction, Atkins said: "not at all.

"Each individual's different, but I think Jake himself - that's the last thing he'd want - to distract from our performance.

"And I think it's a good quality of our playing group is we're mature and we're able to compartmentalise a bit.

"So we can show care for Jake during the week, but we can also put that to the side and perform on the weekend. I think we've done that."

stories.headline: Lando Norris signs new contract to stay at McLaren until at least 2030
stories.summary: Reigning world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a new contract to remain at the team until at least 2030.
stories.body:
Reigning world champion Lando Norris has committed his long-term future to McLaren after signing a new contract to remain at the team until at least 2030.

The deal, which includes one of his title-winning Formula 1 cars as a gift from the team, also has the option of a "multiyear" extension beyond 2030.

Norris, 26, who made his F1 debut with McLaren in 2019, last signed a multiyear contract extension in 2024 that was believed to run until 2027.

Norris' future at McLaren had not looked in doubt and was only cemented by his championship-winning season in 2025, which made him the first driver since Lewis Hamilton in 2008 to win F1's top prize with the team.

The new contract represents a trend in long-term commitments between star drivers and teams in this year's driver market after Max Verstappen committed to Red Bull until 2030 last week and Charles Leclerc signed a new multiyear deal with Ferrari earlier this season.

"McLaren is my home, and I'm very pleased to be signing a new contract to keep me with the team until at least 2030," Norris said. "When I started this journey nine years ago, I was clear about the goals I wanted to achieve: to get McLaren back to the front and to win Championships.

"We've achieved that goal, but we want more, we want to keep on winning, and we know as a team that we're capable of achieving it. I can't wait to get back in the car in Monza and I'm very excited about what the future holds for us, both over the rest of this season, and in the coming years."

Norris' teammate Oscar Piastri extended his contact at the start of the 2025 season and is believed to be committed to the team until at least 2028.

Despite conversations between McLaren's senior management and Verstappen earlier this season, the team has always publicly stated its commitment to Norris and Piastri.

Team principal Andrea Stella used the contract announcement to reiterate his belief that McLaren has one of the strongest driver pairings in F1.

"Lando has been an integral part of McLaren's journey and success over the last nine years, and we are delighted to continue our partnership with him through to at least 2030," Stella said. "He is an exceptional driver, someone who combines outstanding natural speed with maturity, consistency and a strong commitment to McLaren, but above all, he is a special human being who is valued by everyone in the team.

"Since joining McLaren as part of our junior programme, he has grown with us and played a central role in bringing the team back to the front of Formula 1. This extension gives us important continuity and reinforces our confidence in the direction we are taking together. With him and Oscar, we know we can count not only on one of the strongest partnerships but also on one of the most united and close-knit teams in Formula 1."

As part of his new deal, Norris will receive one of the MCL39 cars that he used to secure his first F1 title in 2025.

"This gift serves a lasting reminder of his contribution to the team, in particular his part in securing the team's second consecutive Constructors' title in 2025, while also becoming the team's first Formula 1 Drivers' World Champion since 2008," a team statement said.

stories.headline: Every time Messi scored 4 goals for Barcelona, Inter Miami, Argentina
stories.summary: Lionel Messi grabbed the headlines on Saturday by scoring four goals in Inter Miami's 7-1 win over Montréal. But the feat is nothing new for the GOAT.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi grabbed the headlines on Saturday by scoring four goals for reigning MLS champions Inter Miami CF in their 7-1 win over CF Montréal.

But, for a player who has scored more than 900 goals in a trophy-laden career for Argentina, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami, the feat is nothing new.

In fact, the eight-time winner of the Ballon d'Or has scored a "poker" no fewer than nine times to date. And, on a couple of those occasions, he netted even more than four.

- Messi tracker: Goals, assists, moments for Miami, Argentina

Here are highlights of every single time that the GOAT has done the GOATiest of GOAT things.

1. Barcelona 4-1 Arsenal, Champions League (April 6, 2010)

On a big night for Messi (and a bad one for Arsenal goalkeeper Wojciech Szczesny), Messi hit the first four-goal haul of his career in a UEFA Champions League quarterfinal second leg to move into the ranks of Barcelona's top 10 goal scorers of all-time.

2. Barcelona 5-1 Valencia, LaLiga (Feb. 19, 2012)

Messi had to wait almost two full years for his next "poker," but when it came it was a fine way to mark his 200th appearance in LaLiga for Barça.

3. Barcelona 7-1 Bayer Leverkusen, Champions League (March 7, 2012)

In 2012, Messi was in the best form of his career, and it only took him a couple more weeks to score four goals again. In fact, he was so hot, that he scored five in one match against poor old Leverkusen.

4. Barcelona 4-0 Espanyol, LaLiga (May 5, 2012) (Pep's final game)

Messi capped off an incredible 2011-12 season in the final game by netting his 50th league goal of the campaign. That landmark came as part of his latest four-goal haul, on Pep Guardiola's last match as Barcelona coach.

5. Barcelona 5-1 Osasuna, LaLiga (Jan. 27, 2013)

The following year, Messi scored his 200th LaLiga strike as part of a four-goal salvo. This match was the 11th game of a scoring streak that would eventually extend to 19 matches.

6. Barcelona 6-1 Eibar, LaLiga (Sept. 19, 2017)

Messi knows how to time the delivery of his "poker" performances to hit personal milestones. His next one included his 300th goal scored at Camp Nou.

7. Barcelona 5-0 Eibar, LaLiga (Feb. 22, 2020)

Eibar were again the victims of a Messi scoring blitz in 2020, and this time they could only praise their tormentor. After the match, the club posted on social media: "We suffer you, we put up with you, we endure you. And we have no choice but to stand up and applaud you."

8. Argentina vs. Estonia, international friendly (June 5, 2022)

Why Argentina were playing Estonia in Spanish city of Pamplona, we can't really say. But we do know that he became the first male player to score four goals in a single Champions League game and a senior international match that night. Six months later, he led them to FIFA World Cup glory.

9. Inter Miami CF 7-1 CF Montréal, MLS (Aug. 29, 2026)

It took another four years but, at the age of 39, Messi is still capable of posting those big numbers.

"I'll say it again: I don't have any qualifiers for such soccer beauty," Miami interim coach Guillermo Hoyos said postmatch. "There are so many things combined that leave you at a loss for words, no?

"I don't think he's a normal soccer player."

We couldn't agree more.

stories.headline: Cris Cyborg is still going strong as a force in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: At age 41, PFL women's featherweight champion continues win streak to secure spot in ESPN P4P top 10.
stories.body:
Cris Cyborg is an MMA legend. Period. End of story.

Actually, the Cyborg story continues, even with her being 41 years old and having spent 21 years in the sport. A champion in an unprecedented five fight promotions, she has long been a fixture in the ESPN pound-for-pound women's rankings. And by posting her 30th career victory -- the most ever by a woman in MMA -- at PFL Tampa on Saturday to retain the women's featherweight championship, Cyborg solidified her hold on the No. 3 spot.

It wasn't easy, not like so many past Cyborg fights in which she aggressively bowled over opponents to score quick knockouts. Ketlen Vieira put up a fight, bloodying Cyborg's face and achieving controlling positions on the canvas several times. But Cyborg persevered, nearly doubling Vieira's strike output and earning a unanimous decision win. As a result, the ESPN voting panel kept her right where she was in the top three.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Aug. 26. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko has more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and now she's established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira on Saturday as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 4

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: TBA

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

6. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-2

Last: W (TKO1) vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius, Oct. 18, 2025

Next: Sept. 12 vs. Alexa Grasso

Fiorot has handled everyone the UFC has put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But Fiorot could earn another shot at the belt if she can get past Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

9. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

10. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 17-5-1

Last: W (KO) vs. Maycee Barber, March 28

Next: Sept. 12 vs. Manon Fiorot

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. That made the fight with Barber a must-win, and Grasso came through explosively. Next up is Fiorot, a fellow title contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Valentina Shevchenko; 2. Zhang Weili; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Cris Cyborg; 5. Manon Fiorot; 6. Dakota Ditcheva; 7. Natalia Silva; 8. Erin Blanchfield; 9. Tatiana Suarez; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Ditcheva; 5. Dern; 6. Silva; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Andrew Davis: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Fiorot; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Ditcheva; 9. Suarez; 10. Jandiroba.

Dre Waters: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Fiorot; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Grasso.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Fiorot; 5. Silva; 6. Dern; 7. Blanchfield; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Grasso.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Where does Aspinall go from here?

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

Other fighters receiving votes: Joshua Van and Arman Tsarukyan.

How our panel voted

Dre Waters: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Yan; 4. Dvalishvili; 5. Pantoja; 6. Gaethje; 7. Volkanovski; 8. Topuria; 9. Gane; 10. Van.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Makhachev; 2. Aspinall; 3. Pantoja; 4. Yan; 5. Gaethje; 6. Dvalishvili; 7. Topuria; 8. Gane; 9. Pereira; 10. Volkanovski.

stories.headline: Jets star goalie Connor Hellebuyck confirms trade request
stories.summary: Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.
stories.body:
WINNIPEG, Manitoba -- Three-time Vezina Trophy-winning goaltender Connor Hellebuyck publicly confirmed Thursday that he asked the Winnipeg Jets to trade him.

In a statement released by his agent, Ray Petkau, Hellebuyck said he made the request several months ago and "tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options."

Hellebuyck said he felt it was important to go public because training camp is fast approaching. Camps are set to open in roughly three weeks.

"My position has not changed, and I believe moving on is the best path forward for me and my family," Hellebuyck said. "(I) hope a resolution can be reached soon."

Hellebuyck, 33, has played his entire NHL career with the Jets and was voted MVP in the 2024-25 season. He backstopped the U.S. to the gold medal at the Olympics in February.

A team spokesperson did not immediately respond to a message seeking comment.

Trade rumors swirled about Hellebuyck in late June around the draft, but nothing came to fruition. The Michigan native missed time because of injury and had a career-worst .895 save percentage last season as Winnipeg underachieved expectations and missed the playoffs.

But his track record and body of work are among the best at the position over the past decade. His 345 wins, 2.58 goals-against average and .916 save percentage since entering the league in 2015 are second only to Tampa Bay two-time Stanley Cup champion Andrei Vasilevskiy.

Hellebuyck has not enjoyed the same postseason success as Vasilevskiy and the Lightning. He's 24-34, with the Jets only making it past the second round and into the Western Conference final once, back in 2018.

He signed an eight-year, $59.5 million extension with Winnipeg in October 2023. He's under contract through 2031 at a salary cap hit of $8.5 million.

"Winnipeg has been my home for my entire NHL career, and I will always be grateful for my time there," Hellebuyck said. "I appreciate everything Winnipeg Jets fans have meant to me throughout my career."

stories.headline: Stocks: Dogs gone, Sharks shocked, Phins are up
stories.summary: With the Bulldogs losing and the Rabbitohs and Cowboys winning, the eight teams advancing to the finals are settled. There is still a minor premiership to be decided, but there are now nine teams who can book their end of season trips from next week.
stories.body:
With the Bulldogs losing and the Rabbitohs and Cowboys winning, the eight teams advancing to the finals are settled. There is still a minor premiership to be decided as well as some adjustments to the positions of teams, but there are now nine teams who can book their end of season trips from next week.

Here's whose stocks are up and down after Round 26.

Our footy experts cast their eye over the week's action to find out whose stocks are up -- whether it's a coaching masterstroke or a player having a blinder -- and whose are down.

Brisbane Broncos
Stocks up: The reigning premiers hosted the grand final re-match with both teams 160 minutes of football away from the end of their miserable seasons. The Broncos started with a couple of half breaks before letting the Storm take a tap 10 metres out and waltz through the heart of their defence. It was a sorry sign of what was to come. If you were searching for a positive, they only lost the second half 16-10.

Stocks down: How the mighty have fallen. They say that good defence is an attitude and the Broncos further proved that they have completely given up caring. Scoring tries against the reigning premiers should never be as simple as running hard at some of their best defenders.

-- Darren Arthur

Canberra Raiders
BYE

Canterbury Bankstown Bulldogs
Stocks up: The effort was there. Canterbury stayed within touching distance for most of the night, Jacob Preston worked himself into the ground and Lachlan Galvin kept trying to manufacture opportunities despite Penrith giving him almost no time or space.

Stocks down: Ultimately, this showed the gap between competing with Penrith and actually beating them. The Bulldogs had enough possession and field position to make things interesting, but could never consistently crack the Panthers' defensive line, and the 24-10 defeat effectively ended their finals hopes once the weekend's other results fell into place. After fighting their way back into the race, that's a pretty brutal way for the season to close out.

-- Isaac Issa

Cronulla Sharks
Stocks up: Ronaldo Mulitalo had plenty of great carries, and while it was disallowed, Sione Katoa had one of the coolest put-down attempts you'll ever see. There really wasn't much else to be positive about, although Addin Fonua-Blake did go off with an injury, but returned to the game - which is massive for their finals hopes.

Stocks down: Everything else? Another disappointingly flat showing from a Sharks team that has massively hit the wall since Braydon Trindall went down. A top four spot was up for grabs should they have won their last two games against teams with nothing to play for, but that's gone now. Instead, they're locked into fifth and we get another week of tedious discourse about whether or not they should be allowed to play that finals game at Shark Park.

-- Matt Bungard

Dolphins
Stocks up: This might be their most convincing statement yet. The Dolphins didn't just beat another top-four side - they controlled long stretches of the game and then showed serious resilience when things got messy, surviving periods with 12 and even 11 men on the field. Isaiya Katoa and Kodi Nikorima were excellent in steering them around, Selwyn Cobbo's double gave the Roosters nightmares on the edge and their scramble defence late was outstanding. A 26-12 win moves them above the Roosters and gives them a genuine shot at a home final in their first ever September campaign.

Stocks down: The discipline is the obvious one. Tom Flegler and Morgan Knowles both spending time in the bin could have completely changed the game against a side that executed better with the extra numbers. They survived it this time, but that's not something you want to be testing in finals football.

-- Isaac Issa

Gold Coast Titans
Stocks up: Keano Kini was lightning every time he got half a chance, and Siale Faeamani had some nice carries in his first game in the top grade since round nine. Other than that, it was a pretty by-the-numbers showing from a team that's not offered much in the final month of the season.

Stocks down: It just doesn't feel like anything ever changes with the Titans. They've done enough to avoid the spoon this year, but it's only due to the Dragons being so bad. They're going to finish with the same number of wins as last season and look nowhere near being a finals team in 2027 or beyond. They haven't won more than half their games in a year since 2010.

-- Matt Bungard

Manly Warringah Sea Eagles
Stocks up: From the opening kick-off Manly showed that they meant business. Determined charges into the heart of the Dragons' defence coupled with slick ball movement had the Dragons on their heels. The Sea Eagle had all the ball and ran the Big Red V into the ground, with Saab cashing in on the deft short kicking game of Jamal Fogarty.

Stocks down: It was all for nothing. After such a promising turn around after changing head coach earlier in the year, the Sea Eagles fell agonisingly short of a finals appearance.

-- Darren Arthur

\

Melbourne Storm
Stocks up: The Storm always turn up with the right attitude, regardless of how insignificant the game may be. In the first half they scored some beautifully executed tries against the disinterested Broncos defence. As usual Siulagi Tuimalatu-Brown was dangerous every time he touched the ball on the way to a hat trick.

Stocks down: The win does little to change the fact that they wont be playing finals this tear after appearing in the grand final just under 12 months ago. After going into the break with a healthy lead, they did concede tries in the second half, as the referee awarded multiple set restarts to the Broncos.

-- Darren Arthur

Newcastle Knights
Stocks up: In some ways, this might have been one of Newcastle's more impressive losses. They came flying out of the blocks, then played 67 minutes with 12 men after Saifiti's send-off and somehow continued trading punches with the competition leaders. Fletcher Hunt and Greg Marzhew both finished with doubles, and even after the Warriors took control, Newcastle refused to disappear. With finals already secured, that sort of fight should give Justin Holbrook plenty of confidence heading into September.

Stocks down: Saifiti's tackle changed everything. His forceful high shot knocked Laulilii out of the game and left Newcastle a man short for almost the entire afternoon, while he now faces the prospect of missing finals through suspension. Francis Manuleleua also suffered what appears to be a serious elbow injury, adding another potentially costly blow ahead of September. The Knights showed enormous character, but ultimately they were left paying for one disastrous moment.

-- Isaac Issa

New Zealand Warriors
Stocks up: Talk about passing a depth test. With Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita rested, Jett Cleary walked into halfback on NRL debut and looked completely at home, laying on three try assists as the Warriors fought back from a chaotic start to win 46-32. Newcastle had them 10-0 down inside 10 minutes, but once the game swung, the Warriors found points everywhere, with Jacob Laban grabbing a double and their attack eventually overwhelming a brave 12-man Knights outfit. The win guarantees a home final and sends them back to the top of the ladder - remarkably, still just one point of differential ahead of Penrith.

Stocks down: The circumstances mean Andrew Webster won't be completely thrilled with conceding 32. Even after Jacob Saifiti was sent off in the 13th minute, Newcastle kept finding points and actually went into halftime only two behind. Luke Laulilii also suffered a category-one concussion from the Saifiti shot and will miss next week.

-- Isaac Issa

North Queensland Cowboys
Stocks up: Finals secured, and now playing for placement next week. There's not really a huge difference for them finishing seventh or eighth, so we'll likely see a few players rested next week, which is very valuable heading into a sudden death game on the road. Most importantly, Tom Dearden got through 80 minutes and looked pretty good.

Stocks down: Despite the win it was a pretty error-ridden night, which the Cowboys have had on a few occasions this year. It didn't matter on Saturday, but if they show up to Newcastle or Cronulla with a bad case of the dropsies it will get very ugly for them, very quickly.

-- Matt Bungard

Parramatta Eels
Stocks up: We aren't going to do the 'dark horse for next year' thing with the Eels again, but they have been very competitive in recent weeks and deserved a big win like the one they got today. The back five was superb and Junior Paulo led from the front in a win that few would have seen coming.

Stocks down: What are they going to do with Ronald Volkman next year? I didn't like the Jarome Luai signing because I don't like these one-year deals as a concept (especially for Parra who already did one this year!!) but Volkman has probably been the Eels' best player in this little run to end the season. Where does he fit in the squad in 2027?

-- Matt Bungard

Penrith Panthers
Stocks up: This was classic late-season Penrith - not spectacular for 80 minutes, just relentlessly professional. They completed 38 of 41 sets, Dylan Edwards was immense out the back and Liam Martin's early double helped establish control before Casey McLean put the result beyond doubt late. Nathan Cleary kept them organised throughout, and the 24-10 win sent Penrith back to the top of the ladder, at least momentarily, while guaranteeing them a home final. They just have that familiar look again: calm, clinical and very difficult to drag into a bad game.

Stocks down: Izack Tago leaving the field late after landing awkwardly is something they'll monitor, but otherwise there isn't much here Ivan Cleary will lose sleep over.

-- Isaac Issa

St George Illawarra Dragons
Stocks up: The only real positive out of this performance was that it carried the Dragons a game closer to finishing their miserable season. They can now look forward to using their wooden spoon to mix in the batch of star players they have signed for next year and bake up a much-needed finals appearance.

Stocks down: Eight errors with only 10 completions in the first half told the story of the Dragons' night as they conceded five tries before the break. Things didn't improve into the second half, with the Sea Eagles crossing for another four tries.

-- Darren Arthur

South Sydney Rabbitohs
Stocks up: There was plenty of stuff on the field to like -- David Fifita's solo try against his old team, Latrell Mitchell being back from injury and being better for the run -- but all of that pales in comparison to Jai Arrow's return to the field to a rapturous reception in front of well over 20,000 people on the Gold Coast. It'll be an honour to be there next Friday for game 100.

Stocks down: I feel like I've written this in this exact column a dozen times this year, but once again what was a comfortable lead for Souths got a little bit too close for comfort, as they allowed their opposition to score multiple tries in quick succession. And once again, it coincided with both Brandon Smith and Cam Murray going off the field. Those two came back on and the Bunnies cruised to the finish line, and into their first finals series since 2022.

-- Matt Bungard

Sydney Roosters
Stocks up: James Tedesco's return was a boost and there were still patches when the Roosters threatened to open the Dolphins up, particularly once they had the numerical advantage late.

Stocks down: This was a pretty sobering result for a side that had been pushing for the minor premiership only a week ago. Their attack never really settled, the Dolphins repeatedly won the big moments and, worst of all, Sam Walker left with what has been revealed to be a season-ending syndesmosis injury. After back-to-back defeats and with Walker now gone, the Roosters suddenly have far more to worry about than where they finish inside the top four.

-- Isaac Issa

Wests Tigers
Stocks Up: There was always going to be a comedown after last week's incredible upset win, and this was a pretty respectable performance away from home considering they'd shipped over 140 points in their last three trips to Townsville before this one.

Stocks down: I would really like to have seen a team with nothing to play for show a bit more endeavour in attack - it was a relatively flat showing from the Tigers, and a game we'll all quickly forget - why not chance your arm a bit more?

-- Matt Bungard
